Edwards Nguyen

I'm a student at the Gwinnett School of Mathematics, Science, and Technology with a growing interest in computer science and computational science, especially simulation. That interest led me to found a podcast, What the Model Misses, and a children's book, What the Zoo Misses, both built around one question: what does a model leave out? Along the way I've learned that the best models are the ones you can explain plainly, and that the deciding of what to leave in or out is where the real science happens.

I want to study computer science and data science, then go on to earn a PhD building models of the people cities forget.

What the Model Misses

Podcast hosted by Edwards Nguyen

Format
Podcast
Host
Edwards Nguyen
Updated
September 2026

Abstract

Every model is a simplification. To represent a complex system, a model must decide what to include and, by necessity, what to omit. What the Model Misses examines those omissions.

Hosted by Edwards Nguyen, a high school student, the podcast presents extended conversations with researchers and faculty from Johns Hopkins University, Columbia University, the University of Michigan, University College London, and other leading institutions. The series spans eight fields: geography, neuroscience, human collaboration with artificial intelligence, language, culture, robotics, genetics, and education. Each conversation pursues a single guiding question: what do our models fail to capture about the systems they claim to represent?

The answers reach further than one might expect. Guests explain why artificial intelligence still struggles to understand humor that depends on culture, why an identical coding task can cost thirty times more when it is run a second time, why the brain's "wiring diagrams" omit an entire class of connections, and why the central limitation of urban models lies not in data but in theory.

Eight fields, eight blind spots, and the scholars who have devoted their careers to understanding them. What the Model Misses offers listeners rare access to research conversations that seldom reach a general audience.
